setup: Bar end in a landmine or a padded corner
Feet a bit wider than your shoulders
Hold the bar end at chest height, arms long
execution: Turn your hips and chest together
Sweep the bar down toward one hip
Brace and bring it back over the top
Move slowly and stop the bar each side
faults: Don't let your arms bend to muscle it
Don't let the bar drag you round
Don't twist from the lower back alone

notes: Start light: the bar's momentum grows quickly at the bottom of each arc.
Let the feet and hips turn with the bar so the lower back isn't twisted on its own.
Make sure the landmine sleeve or corner is secure and the space around you is clear.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

guideBrief.cameraNote: Front view at chest height, figure facing the camera with the landmine anchor on the floor behind it. The bar end's arc from hip to hip over the head line must be visible.

keyPositions.label: Centre
keyPositions.describe: Standing tall, feet wider than shoulders, knees soft. Both hands on the bar end at about chest height, arms long. Hips and chest square to the bar.

keyPositions.label: Side
keyPositions.describe: Hips and chest turned to one side together, bar end lowered toward the outside of that hip. Back foot pivoting on the ball. Arms still long.

keyPositions.label: Other side
keyPositions.describe: Bar brought back up over the centre and down to the other hip in a rainbow arc; the mirror of the previous position.

ikHints: Bar end stays in both hands
Far end of the bar stays fixed in the landmine
guideBrief.barPath: A rainbow arc from one hip, up past chest height, down to the other hip
doNotShow: Feet planted while only the waist twists
